ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ with $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=70^\circ$. Points $O$ and $D$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $AB$, respectively. A circle is drawn with $O$ as the center and $OD$ as the radius, intersecting $AB$ at another point $E$ and intersecting $AC$ at points $G$ and $F$. What is the degree measure of $\angle DOE + \angle FOG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $O$ and $D$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $AB$ respectively, and $AB=AC$,\\
it follows that $OD\parallel AC$, and $OG=OD= \frac{1}{2}AC= \frac{1}{2}AB$,\\
therefore, $\angle ODE=\angle A=70^\circ$, and $OG\parallel AB$,\\
thus, $\angle OGF=\angle A=70^\circ$,\\
since $OE=OD=OG=OF$,\\
it implies that $\angle ODE=\angle OED=70^\circ$, $\angle OFG=\angle OGF=70^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle DOD=\angle GOF=40^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle DOE+\angle FOG=\boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an isosceles triangle ABC, A is above, B and C are at the two ends of the base, and O is located on the base BC. D and E are located on side AB, with D closer to A and E closer to B; the circle with O as the center passes through D and E, and intersects side AC at G and F, with G closer to A and F closer to C. The radii OD, OE, OG, and OF are also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: Because O is the midpoint of BC, and D is the midpoint of AB, in triangle ABC, OD is a midline, so OD ∥ AC, and OD = AC/2. Also because E is on the circle with O as the center and OD as the radius, OE = OD. Since DE is on AB, and DO ∥ AC, therefore ∠ODE is equal to ∠BAC, namely 70°. In triangle ODE, OD = OE, so the base angles ∠ODE = ∠OED = 70°, hence ∠DOE = 180° - 70° - 70° = 40°. Next let M be the midpoint of AC. Because O is the midpoint of BC, OM is a midline of triangle ABC, OM ∥ AB, and OM = AB/2. Also AB = AC, so OM = AC/2 = OD, therefore M is on this circle. Combining with the image, it can be known that this circle intersection point on AC closer to A is G, so OG ∥ AB. Because GF is on AC, and OG ∥ AB, ∠OGF = ∠BAC = 70°. Also OG = OF are both radii of the circle, so triangle OGF is an isosceles triangle, ∠OFG = ∠OGF = 70°, and thus ∠FOG = 180° - 70° - 70° = 40°. Therefore ∠DOE + ∠FOG = 40° + 40° = 80°.
